D4·qgqr — 2026-09-15
chose: 1.2 implementation rulings within D2/D3: (1) `ok: true` is written EXPLICITLY on every successful command_run/file_touched, not just `ok: false` on failures — so absence means "an engine or host that predates capture", never "succeeded"; a reader can tell unknown from success. (2) The failed half of the record is a new PostToolUseFailure shim (matcher Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash → `sofar event post-tool-failure`), installed by `sofar init` as the sixth shim: Claude Code fires PostToolUse only on exit 0, so until now a failing `npm test` left no event at all. (3) The MCP server writes its own `mcp_call` row per call (success or typed rejection) since the PostToolUse matcher never sees mcp__sofar__* calls. (4) Retention mechanics: 90-day sweep at most once a day per clone (meta.json), 8 MiB per-file cap compacting to half, one stat per write. (5) Row `kind` set: tool_outcome, tool_failure, mcp_call, injection (SessionStart bytes + repo-memory bytes as the size half of a memory-use signal).
over: Recording only `ok: false` (absence = success); a consumer inferring failure from output text; putting exit-code parsing of the host's prose `error` line into the event; a sweep on every write.
because: Verified against Claude Code hook docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, checked 2026-09-15): PostToolUse fires only on success, PostToolUseFailure carries structured `exit_code` and `stderr` for Bash. In this session's own transcript the Bash tool_response had NO exit_code (stdout, stderr, interrupted, isImage, noOutputExpected), so `exit` on a success event is host-dependent and 1.3 must mark it so. Explicit true costs ~10 bytes per event and buys the unknown/success distinction D2 (4) requires. A per-write sweep would read the whole file inside the 100ms shim budget; a daily sweep costs one stat.
